commit_conventions.observations: Titles are short imperative or descriptive phrases in lower case, usually with a conventional-commit style type (feat:, fix:, docs:, chore:) or a component prefix (actions:, tests:, templates:, goreleaser:, Makefile:, run/qemu:, luks:); 26 of 100 titles have no prefix, so a prefix is customary but not enforced, and no title length limit is kept (a few early titles exceed 100 characters). Use feat: for the riscv64 platform support so it appears in the goreleaser changelog, and actions:, tests:, docs: or goreleaser: for CI, test, documentation and release-list commits, which the changelog filters out. Bodies are optional; when present they are short bullet lists. Nearly every commit ends with a Signed-off-by trailer, and the maintainer additionally asks external contributors for cryptographically signed (verified) commits and for squashing fixups; main of linka-cloud/d2vm is a protected branch. Issues are referenced as 'closes #N' in the PR body or '(closes #N)' in the title. Two documentation commits carry a 'skip-checks: true' trailer or a '[skip ci]' title marker; do not use these for code changes. Maintainer feature PRs contain one to four logical commits (PR 44: 1, PR 91: 2, PR 43: 4); keep each commit a self-contained unit and never leave fixup commits.

dependency_graph.assessment: The tool succeeded but the graph has no node for d2vm under any identity: no vcs:Repository whose IRI or literals contain d2vm (query repo), no core:identityName equal to d2vm, go.linka.cloud/d2vm, linka-cloud/d2vm or luhenry/d2vm (query ident), and no pkg:golang purl at all (query golang returns 0), so the graph does not cover the Go module ecosystem. Direct, transitive and reverse dependency edges of d2vm are therefore unavailable; this is missing data, not an empty dependency set, and no edge is inferred from it. What the graph does confirm (queries hosttools, grubarch, riscv64_hosttools) is the Ubuntu resolute riscv64 availability of the host tools and guest packages d2vm shells out to or installs: util-linux, udev, parted, kpartx, e2fsprogs, dosfstools, mount, tar, cryptsetup-bin, qemu-utils, qemu-system-riscv, qemu-system-misc, docker.io, golang-go 1.26, grub-common, grub2-common, grub-efi-riscv64, grub-efi-riscv64-bin, linux-image-virtual and linux-image-generic all have riscv64 binaries; qemu-efi-riscv64 exists as an architecture-independent package; extlinux exists for amd64 only, which matches the code restricting syslinux to x86_64. Build dependencies from the checkout (go.mod, not in the graph): 17 direct Go modules (go-containerregistry, hcloud-go, pkg/sftp, logrus, cobra, pflag, testify, sparsecat, go.linka.cloud/console, multierr, x/crypto, x/sys, datasize, go-humanize, fatih/color, uuid, godotenv) and 34 indirect ones, all pure Go; the build sets CGO_ENABLED=0 and the repository contains no assembly, cgo or architecture build tags. A local cross build with GOARCH=riscv64 of ./cmd/d2vm at 7184ff1 produced a static riscv64 executable, which shows every direct and transitive Go dependency compiles for linux/riscv64. Runtime dependencies are external programs (docker, parted, kpartx, mkfs, qemu-img, cryptsetup, grub-install inside the guest chroot, optional qemu-system and VirtualBox), covered by the distribution evidence above. Test dependencies: testify, docker with binfmt, qemu-system and UEFI firmware. No reverse dependencies are known from the graph; pkg.go.dev lists the module as a command-line tool.

There is no assembly or cgo; the architecture-specific source is a set of Go switches and Dockerfile templates. builder.go (NewBuilder) and cmd/d2vm/flags.go (validateFlags, flag help) reject every platform except linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 and need a linux/riscv64 case that defaults to and only allows grub-efi, like arm64. grub_efi.go builds the grub target from the arch string (riscv64-efi is valid) and grub_common.go holds the shared config; grub.go, grub_bios.go and syslinux.go already refuse non x86 arches and bootloader.go defines the provider interface; config.go holds the kernel cmdline (console device) and dockerfile.go passes template data and may need to expose the architecture. templates/debian.Dockerfile hardcodes linux-image-amd64 and, like templates/ubuntu.Dockerfile, maps every non x86_64 machine to arm64 package names; templates/alpine.Dockerfile installs linux-virt, which Alpine does not build for riscv64 (linux-lts is); templates/centos.Dockerfile installs grub2-efi-x64. pkg/qemu/qemu.go and cmd/d2vm/run/qemu.go lack riscv64 in the default-arch and GOARCH switches, use -cpu host even without KVM, select q35 for unknown arches and pass firmware with -bios, while the riscv64 virt machine needs edk2 on pflash; pkg/qemu/config.go carries the options. cmd/d2vm/run/util.go and hetzner.go select the embedded sparsecat by arch. pkg/docker/docker.go passes --platform to docker and names the d2vm image; version.go derives the default platform from GOARCH; convert.go, convert_options.go and container_disk.go carry the platform string; qemu.sh hardcodes qemu-system-x86_64.

proposal.rationale: Develop. d2vm is a pure Go command (CGO_ENABLED=0, no assembly, no cgo, no build tags) that already cross-compiles to a static linux/riscv64 binary at main 7184ff1, but that binary is useless as shipped: version.go makes linux/riscv64 its default platform and both cmd/d2vm/flags.go and builder.go reject every platform other than linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, pkg/qemu and cmd/d2vm/run/qemu.go have no riscv64 case, the Dockerfile templates compute amd64 or arm64 package names only, and .goreleaser.yaml releases amd64 and arm64 only. A concrete bounded patch exists and follows the accepted arm64 precedent (linka-cloud/d2vm PR 44, issue 40): add linux/riscv64 as an EFI-only platform whose bootloader defaults to and is restricted to grub-efi (grub target riscv64-efi), make the Ubuntu, Debian and Alpine templates choose riscv64 kernel and grub packages (linux-image-virtual, linux-image-riscv64, linux-lts; grub-efi-riscv64-bin or grub-efi, all verified to exist), teach pkg/qemu and d2vm run qemu the riscv64 virt machine with edk2 on pflash and a TCG-safe CPU model, add riscv64 to the goreleaser goarch list, add an emulated riscv64 e2e case on the existing shared ubuntu-latest host, and update README, docs/content and the generated CLI reference. Every dependency this needs is available: Go 1.25 for riscv64, golang:1.25 and ubuntu base images, tonistiigi/binfmt with riscv64, qemu-system-riscv64, qemu-efi-riscv64 firmware, and riscv64 manifests for ubuntu:22.04, ubuntu:24.04, debian:13 and alpine:3.23. There is no prior riscv64 work, request or objection in luhenry/d2vm (no issues, PRs, tags or Actions runs) or in linka-cloud/d2vm (42 issues and 51 PRs reviewed); the maintainer's recorded constraints are e2e coverage, minimal diffs, one template per distribution family, unchanged behaviour for existing platforms and squashed signed commits, all of which the proposed shape satisfies. The requester, who owns the upstream repository, explicitly asked for the riscv64 port of this Go project to be planned. Close is not applicable (not a PyPI project, riscv64 served nowhere) and park is not warranted because nothing blocks a first patch. The riscv64-draft branch was not consulted, as the tracking issue requires.

proposal.risks: 1. e2e duration: converting under qemu-user and booting under TCG on ubuntu-latest is slow; the fixed two minute login timeout in e2e_test.go will need a per-platform value and the riscv64 rows should be limited to a few images. 2. pkg/qemu passes firmware with -bios, which on riscv64 is the SBI slot; edk2 must be attached as pflash (code and a writable copy of vars), and -cpu host must not be used without KVM. 3. grub-install --target=riscv64-efi runs inside the guest chroot through binfmt on an amd64 host; the removable path is BOOTRISCV64.EFI and the kernel must be an EFI-stub image, which distribution kernels are, but the generated grub.cfg and console (ttyS0 on virt) need verification per distribution. 4. goreleaser v1.10.1 with goarch riscv64 across windows and darwin must be checked with make build-snapshot; add an ignore list if it fails. 5. When d2vm runs unprivileged or on a non-Linux host it re-executes inside linkacloud/d2vm, which has no riscv64 image; native root use on riscv64 works, the container path does not until a riscv64 image exists (docker:dind lacks riscv64). 6. The Debian template installs linux-image-amd64 unconditionally, which looks broken for arm64 too; fixing it by deriving the package from the architecture changes arm64 behaviour and must be kept minimal. 7. docs-up-to-date fails unless docs/content/reference is regenerated with the built binary on amd64 (the default --platform value in the generated help is the build host platform). 8. The linka-cloud maintainer has stated no position on riscv64 and accepts only targets he can test; open PR 92 edits the same boot loader files and would conflict with a later submission there. 9. No CI evidence exists yet in luhenry/d2vm; the first run establishes the baseline, including jobs that depend on third-party images (centos:8, kali) unrelated to this change.
proposal.target_matrix: Host: linux/riscv64 d2vm binary released by goreleaser (static, CGO disabled, default GORISCV64 rva20u64). Guest platform: --platform linux/riscv64 with bootloader grub-efi only (GPT, FAT32 ESP, removable riscv64-efi GRUB image), optional split boot and LUKS as on arm64. Distributions to enable and test first: ubuntu:24.04 and ubuntu:22.04, debian:13, alpine:3.23 (linux-lts); Rocky Linux 10 has a riscv64 image and can follow through the RHEL-family template; debian:12, almalinux, centos:8, rockylinux:9 and kali have no riscv64 base image and must be skipped for this platform. Run: d2vm run qemu --arch riscv64 on machine virt with OpenSBI default firmware plus edk2 on pflash, KVM when host matches, TCG otherwise. Out of scope: syslinux, grub-bios and grub (BIOS+EFI) boot loaders, d2vm run hetzner and vbox, the Homebrew formula, and (initially) the Docker image.

docker:dind lists amd64, arm/v6, arm/v7, arm64/v8, ppc64le, s390x and no riscv64, so COPY --from=docker:dind cannot resolve on riscv64.
Docker publishes static CLI binaries in a riscv64 directory next to aarch64 and x86_64; together with the Ubuntu docker.io package this is an alternative source for the docker CLI in a riscv64 image.
debian:13 has linux/riscv64; debian:12 does not (riscv64 became a Debian release architecture with trixie).
alpine:3.23 has linux/riscv64.
rockylinux:9 has no riscv64; the latest and 10 tags (also rockylinux/rockylinux:10) do. almalinux:10, centos:8 and kalilinux/kali-rolling have no riscv64 manifest.
The binfmt image used by docker/setup-qemu-action includes a riscv64 emulator, so the existing CI step already enables linux/riscv64 containers on ubuntu-latest.
Ubuntu 24.04 ships linux-image-virtual for riscv64 (6.8.0-31.31.1), so the Ubuntu template's kernel package resolves on riscv64.
grub-efi-riscv64-bin exists in jammy, noble and resolute; the template must select riscv64 instead of falling through to arm64.
edk2 firmware for the QEMU virt machine: /usr/share/qemu-efi-riscv64/RISCV_VIRT_CODE.fd and RISCV_VIRT_VARS.fd, installable on the amd64 runner (architecture all).
qemu-system-misc (qemu-system-riscv64) is available on amd64 and riscv64 hosts; ci.yaml already installs the qemu-system metapackage.
Debian 13 kernel metapackage for riscv64 exists; the Debian template hardcodes linux-image-amd64 and must derive the name from the architecture.
Debian 13 ships grub-efi-riscv64-bin 2.12.

Alpine 3.23 builds linux-virt for x86, x86_64, armv7 and aarch64 but not riscv64; riscv64 has linux-lts 6.18 instead, and grub-efi 2.12 is built for riscv64. The Alpine template needs a kernel flavour choice for riscv64.
Go supports riscv64 as rv64g; since Go 1.23 the RVA20U64 mandatory extensions are required. Go 1.25 from go.mod and CI therefore targets linux/riscv64 natively.

goreleaser builds accept riscv64 in goarch (with an optional goriscv64 level in newer versions); the project pins v1.10.1, whose behaviour for windows and darwin combined with riscv64 must be checked with make build-snapshot and an ignore list added if needed.
The riscv64 virt machine boots OpenSBI as default -bios and expects edk2 on the pflash devices (pflash0 code, pflash1 vars), not through -bios; pkg/qemu must grow pflash support for an EFI boot test.

data.summary: d2vm (go.linka.cloud/d2vm; luhenry/d2vm main is identical to linka-cloud/d2vm main at 7184ff1) is a pure Go tool that turns Docker images into bootable VM disk images. It supports linux/amd64 (syslinux, grub, grub-bios, grub-efi) and, since PR 44, linux/arm64 with grub-efi only. It has no riscv64 support and no riscv64 history: no issue, PR, CI job, release artifact or document mentions RISC-V. The code already compiles for linux/riscv64, but the resulting binary rejects its own default platform, the templates pick amd64 or arm64 packages, the QEMU runner has no riscv64 machine and goreleaser releases amd64 and arm64 only. All prerequisites exist on riscv64 (Go, base images, binfmt, qemu-system-riscv64, edk2 firmware, kernels and grub-efi packages for Ubuntu, Debian 13 and Alpine). Decision: develop, admission class architecture_correctness, following the arm64 precedent: add linux/riscv64 as an EFI-only platform across the platform switches, templates, QEMU runner, goreleaser goarch list, documentation and generated CLI reference, with an emulated riscv64 e2e case on the existing shared ubuntu-latest CI host. No ecosystem report and no project-graph node exist for d2vm; both absences are documented. The riscv64-draft branch named in the tracking issue was not consulted.

summary: d2vm is a pure Go Docker-to-VM image builder with amd64 and arm64 (grub-efi) support and no riscv64 support or history upstream. It cross-compiles for linux/riscv64 today, but the platform switches (builder.go, cmd/d2vm/flags.go), Dockerfile templates, QEMU runner and goreleaser goarch list exclude riscv64. Plan decision: develop, class architecture_correctness, adding linux/riscv64 as an EFI-only platform after the arm64 precedent (linka-cloud/d2vm PR 44), with templates, pkg/qemu, release list, docs and an emulated e2e case on the shared ubuntu-latest host. All needed toolchain, image and distribution package dependencies exist for riscv64; docker:dind and several distribution base images do not. No ecosystem report or project-graph node exists for d2vm. The riscv64-draft branch was not consulted.
